changed_steps.step: Tell whether this job stopped at its time limit

lesson.summary: The first approve-merge run after #648 never reached the changed step: the ship job succeeded, so the time-limit step, which runs only when the job is cancelled, was skipped as designed, and nothing needs doing.
lesson.detail: Pull request #648 (ticket #642) added the "Tell whether this job stopped at its time limit" step to the ship and send-back jobs of approve-merge. The step runs only under `if: cancelled()`, and it reports whether a cancelled job used up its whole timeout, so that the retro step starts only for a real time-limit stop. In run 45064560587, ship ran its merge-button follow-up step and succeeded. That made the time-limit step and the retro step skip, and test-main and send-back were skipped too. The run never reached the change, so it neither confirms nor contradicts what #648 claimed. Adam's one assumption, about Vercel Web Analytics quota on preview deployments, concerns the setup templates and not this workflow.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run succeeded and cost $0 and 0 turns.

lesson.saves: Nothing: the run cost $0 and had no friction to save.
